problem: Existing VLN methods predict planar waypoints or discrete actions and delegate execution to velocity-command controllers, so they cannot reason about whole-body traversability (arm, torso, gait) in cluttered 3D scenes. Humanoid RL traversal methods are task-specific and do not scale to long-horizon language-guided navigation.
motivation: Humanoids have articulated bodies whose configuration is part of the navigation problem: a path valid in 2D may be infeasible for the body. Large-scale, dynamically feasible whole-body navigation data does not exist, and mocap plus retargeting is costly and degrades motion quality.
key_idea: A single VLA maps language plus egocentric RGB directly to 29-DoF whole-body joint-space action chunks, trained on simulated data from a Plan-Edit-Track pipeline and executed by a general pretrained tracker (SONIC).
insight: Predicting whole-body actions rather than planar trajectories is what makes the policy robust under physical execution: Ours-2D with the Unitree controller drops to 26.67 SR / 8.34 SPL, while the full model reaches 52.89 / 40.18. Component ablations on augmented scenes show training-time RTC is critical (SR 43.75 to 10.94 without it), and obstacle-aware motion editing reduces collisions (CR 20.60 without vs 9.90 with). Swapping the tracker to ScaleBFM stays close, so the design is not tied to SONIC.
method: Environment augmentation: 578 filtered VLNVerse/SAGE-3D scenes (205+373, filtered by Gemini 2.5 Flash) get trajectory-conditioned stride (low), sidle (side pair) and squat (overhead) obstacles, with language prompts regenerated by Gemini.
Plan: A* on a 2D grid with an SDF-based obstacle-aware cost, plus a rule-based 90° yaw rewrite in narrow passages for side-walking; velocity commands go to SONIC to produce natural gaits.

Edit: whole-body IK with HumanoidPF-style repulsive potential fields applied as SoftMimic pseudo-forces on key links, a crouch controller with look-ahead and a virtual head barrier, and gait adaptation that retargets footholds and swing arcs for step-over.

Track/filter: edited references are tracked by SONIC in MuJoCo, and colliding or failing trajectories are discarded; the collision-free references (not the tracked motions) are used as supervision. This yields 64,633 trajectories for 211 GPU-hours.
System-2: Qwen2.5-VL-7B warm-started from InternVLA-N1, taking front and downward views stacked vertically, with BATS history sampling and grid pooling, co-tuned with VideoQA (text CE loss).

System-1: MM-DiT flow-matching action expert predicting 29 joint angles, 6D base rotation (yaw relative to the chunk start) and planar delta auxiliaries, trained with training-time RTC using a random committed prefix; w_FM=20.

System-0 and deployment: SONIC tracker on a Jetson Orin NX (about 200 Hz), VLA on a server every 0.5 s (15 actions at 30 Hz, resampled to 50 Hz); simulation uses MuJoCo physics with an IsaacSim digital-twin camera.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (warm-started from InternVLA-N1, fine-tuned) + MM-DiT flow-matching action expert + SONIC tracker (pretrained, frozen)
setting.training_data: 64,633 synthetic whole-body trajectories from PET on VLNVerse and SAGE-3D (original + augmented scenes) plus VideoQA co-tuning; no real-world data; full-parameter tuning on 896 A100 GPU-hours
setting.observation: front and downward egocentric RGB history + whole-body joint proprioception
setting.action_space: 29-DoF joint-angle chunks + 6D base rotation, streamed to a whole-body tracker
setting.privileged: none at test time (RGB only; the HumanoidPF baseline uses LiDAR)

numbers.extra: only method with physical low-level control; baselines evaluated with teleportation

results: On VLNVerse, TANGO gets the highest SR (54.69 seen / 52.89 unseen) and lowest NE despite real physical control, with SPL 40.18 below RDP's 42.72 on val-unseen. On augmented cluttered scenes it beats InternVLA-N1 + HumanoidPF (SR 41.88, CR 15.81) with SR 43.75 and CR 9.90 using only RGB. In the real world it gets 10/15 in cluttered 3D scenes vs 6/15 for InternVLA-N1 + Unitree WBC.
limitations: Capability is bounded by the low-level tracker (e.g. stairs are infeasible), and it tends toward conservative, less direct paths (lower SPL).
RGB-only input may struggle in visually ambiguous or low-light scenes; depth or LiDAR is left for future work.
Real-world evaluation is small (15 trials per setting), and the cluttered instructions explicitly state the required behavior.
